I can reproduce it (Ubuntu 14.04 too) but it doesn't seem to be related to 0.17dev0. I get the same error with scikit-learn 0.15.2 and 0.16.0.

I can reproduce DonBeo's error with sklearn 0.16.1.

Also, I have experienced a similar issue with `GridSearchCV` and Pandas data frames (see below).
Oddly, the behavior seems to depend on the shape of the data set. A small data set runs fine whereas a larger data set does not.

A [suggested workaround](https://github.com/pydata/pandas/issues/9928) is to use `gs2.fit(X.values, y.values)` below.

``` python
import numpy as np
#from sklearn.linear_model import LassoLarsCV
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.grid_search import GridSearchCV

# n, p = 1453, 1931  # Runs
n, p = 58509, 1247  # Fails

X = np.random.normal(0, 1, (n, p))
y = X[:, 1] + X[:, 2] + np.random.normal(0, 1, n)

X = pd.DataFrame(X)
y = pd.DataFrame(y)

model = RandomForestRegressor()
parameters = {'n_estimators': [10, 50, 100]}
gs1 = GridSearchCV(model, param_grid=parameters, n_jobs=1)
gs1.fit(X, y)
print('Single job succeeded')
gs2 = GridSearchCV(model, param_grid=parameters, n_jobs=3)
gs2.fit(X, y)
print('three jobs succeeded -- I never got to this')
```

I think the problem is in the slicing of the data, which doesn't call `check_array` as we don't want to convert data to an array in the cross-validation / grid-search part.
If the data is a large list of strings, that would be pretty bad. Also, someone might want to use a pd dataframe as input in their estimator, and converting to numpy array early would be bad for that.
So safe_indexing seems to break for pandas dataframes sometimes...
So the problem is with `return X.iloc[indices]`
I opened an issue at pandas: https://github.com/pydata/pandas/issues/10043 I don't understand the behavior, maybe using `iloc` is not the right way to slice.
@ogrisel @GaelVaroquaux could either of you explain why X is not writable? This is multi-processing, and X is copied, right?
This is actually a Cython issue, there are no read-only cython buffers, so input on why there is a read-only flag would be great.

By default the automated memory mapping feature of joblib is converting all big arrays into read-only  `np.memmap` instances in the multiprocessing workers.

There exists two additional modes for memory mapping:
- read-write: but we don't want to use that otherwise it would mean that concurrent workers could corrupt each other input data,
- copy-on-write: to avoid memory copies when the input data is untouched and to automatically copy memory pages whenever they are accessed in write mode to simulate memory isolation.

Ideally we would therefore use copy-on-write as a reasonable default. Unfortunately the support for the copy-on-write mode under Windows is half broken and tends to crash on large data: see joblib/joblib#150.

In this case we should separate the issue with `LassoLarsCV` from the one related to slicing a pandas data frame backed by a memory mapped array in read-only mode. For the original problem with `LassoLarsCV` I think it's a design problem in this class (or its internals): no estimator should try to edit the input data by default, unless the user explicitly pass `copy=False`. I will try to have deeper look.

For the problem happening when using grid search on a large data frame, I think it better to track the discussion in pydata/pandas#10043 as I think this is might be a problem with the way  `pandas.DataFrame.iloc` is currently implemented.

Side note:  joblib uses memory mapping to share arrays between Python processes (forked by multiprocessing when doing a `GridSearchCV` or `LassoLarsCV` with `n_jobs != 1`). memory mapping is not used when using joblib in threading mode as it the case in `RandomForestClassifier` with `n_jobs != 1`. Threading used shared memory by default but unfortunately the threading mode can only be used efficiently by Cython code that releeases the GIL, this is why we cannot use it for general utilities like `GridSearchCV`.

Oh, I didn't realize the lasso issue was a different one. That should be easy to fix, though.
I think pandas can not fix this until it is fixed upstream in cython, and we can't really wait for it. I'll code up a fix.
